Uniformly for c<=sigma<=1, it gives the 2k-th time-averaged moment of P_X as a(k,sigma)F_X(k,sigma)(1+O_k(1/log X)); a(k,sigma) is the displayed Euler product, F_X is piecewise defined, and a(k,1/2)=a(k).

The gain is a bridge from divisor and zero data to a product-ready logarithm; the cost is dependence on absolute convergence, excluded evaluation points, and carefully separated branch conventions.

A symmetric limiting convention defines log zeta when the horizontal line passes through a zero, while a distinct symmetric convention defines U when its E1 argument lies on the branch cut; the representation excludes the pole and zeros as evaluation points.

Time averaging then converts the analytic product into a gcd-weighted main double sum, so shared divisors become the arithmetic correlation kernel; evaluating that main sum is deliberately left to the subsequent gcd decomposition.
